title: Open Problem (linear-time 3-coloring output)
statement_text: Does there exist a linear-time algorithm to output a 3-coloring of a triangle-free graph embedded in a fixed surface (with a bounded number of precolored boundary vertices), using ideas similar to those of the authors' linear-time algorithm deciding 3-colorability of such graphs?
context_text: Here a surface is a compact connected 2-manifold, possibly with boundary (obtained from the sphere by adding handles and crosscaps and removing disjoint open discs); graphs are embedded in it, and vertices lying on the boundary are boundary vertices. For a fixed surface $\Sigma$ and integer $k$, the input is a triangle-free graph $G$ embedded in $\Sigma$ with at most $k$ boundary vertices together with a precoloring $\psi$ of the boundary vertices with colours $\{1,2,3\}$, and the task is to find a proper 3-coloring of $G$ extending $\psi$ (if one exists). 3-colorability of planar graphs is NP-complete, whereas Grötzsch's theorem says planar triangle-free graphs are 3-colorable. Building on their earlier result that in a 4-critical graph on a fixed surface almost all faces have length 4, and on their linear-time 3-coloring algorithm for quadrangulations, the authors give a linear-time algorithm deciding whether such a precoloring extends to a 3-coloring (it only decides whether there is a 4-critical subgraph, without producing a coloring), and a quadratic-time algorithm that also outputs a 3-coloring in the affirmative case, by reducing in quadratic time to graphs of girth at least 5. They believe a linear-time algorithm outputting a coloring exists, using ideas similar to those of the decision algorithm, but note significant technical challenges and leave it open; even for planar graphs, a linear-time algorithm finding the 3-coloring guaranteed by Grötzsch's theorem was found only recently (Dvořák, Kawarabayashi, Thomas).
notes: Stated in running prose in the introduction: 'we believe that there exists a linear-time algorithm to output a 3-coloring using ideas similar to those of Theorem 1.3; however, there are significant technical challenges in designing it and we leave this as an open problem.' No labelled theorem environment.
paper_title: Three-coloring triangle-free graphs on surfaces VII. A linear-time algorithm
